clue.text: Eleven represented by Cleopatra maybe

definitions.meaning: a football side of eleven players: this one is a Scottish club based in Dumfries
Cleopatra ruled Egypt, a monarch of a southern land, so she fits the description

explanation.surface: A team of eleven performers in a play portrayed by the actress playing Cleopatra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eleven' is a team in sport: Queen of the South is a Scottish football club. 'maybe' marks Cleopatra as one example of a southern royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Football sides are called elevens, and this club's name doubles as a title for a southern female monarch.

clue.text: Accommodate some US money

definitions.meaning: to ... troops is to lodge or house them

explanation.surface: Find room for some American cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge soldiers is to give them quarters, and the US 25-cent coin is a fourth of a dollar.

clue.text: Entertainer shortly to be found in Monaco?

indicators.note: the clue's 'shortly' points to an abbreviation, here one which, when spoken, is a showbiz word

parts.note: MC is the international vehicle registration code for Monaco

explanation.surface: A performer briefly turning up in the principality.
explanation.walkthrough: MC (Monaco's car code) is also short for master of ceremonies; said out loud, the two letters give the written-out spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere or host of a show is a kind of entertainer.

clue.text: Very evil fellow cutting miserly promises of payment

indicators.note: the fellow's letter cuts into the word for miserly, splitting it

parts.note: near means stingy or mean with money
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A wicked man who reneges on a stingy set of debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked or villainous behaviour is extremely evil.

clue.text: Got in an agitated state describing guitar?

definitions.meaning: a guitar neck has frets, raised ridges, so it is fitted with them

explanation.surface: Someone became anxious when talking about a guitar.
explanation.definitionFit: To worry is to fret; a guitar with ridges on its fingerboard is furnished with frets.

clue.text: DA, perhaps, is broadcast before start of case in small dwelling

indicators.note: the broadcast word and first letter sit inside the small dwelling

parts.note: a hut is a small, simple house

indicators.note: the broadcast word comes ahead of the initial letter

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word case

explanation.surface: A district attorney is on the radio before opening a case, from a modest home.
explanation.walkthrough: DA here is not a lawyer but a duck's arse, a 1950s slicked-back hairstyle. 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The duck's arse is a style of hairdressing, so it is one example of a cut.

clue.text: Risqué film set in the Seychelles

indicators.note: the film is placed inside the code for the islands

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
a pic is an informal word for a film

explanation.surface: A racy movie shot on the Indian Ocean islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly indecent or saucy material is described as racy or hot.

clue.text: Ban a tour weaving around Latin capital

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
weaving suggests the letters move in and out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A prohibition on a tour that winds about a Latin-speaking city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weaving' rearranges BANATOUR into UANBATOR, and 'around' wraps it about L.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the seat of government of Mongolia, its chief city.

clue.text: Dance instruction for Epsom agricultural worker?

definitions.meaning: Epsom Downs is a racecourse on chalk hills; a farmhand there might be told to till the grassy hill with his tool

explanation.surface: A dance step given to a farm labourer at the Surrey racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs, in Surrey, England, is where the Derby is run; a down is an open chalk hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A barn-dance or square-dance party in rural America goes by this name.

clue.text: Leading hostile figure deployed a force around hospital

indicators.note: the reordered letters enclose the hospital abbreviation
troops deployed are spread into a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A top enemy commander sent troops round a field hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deployed' rearranges A FORCE into ARCFOE, and 'around' puts it about H.
explanation.definitionFit: A chief enemy is the principal adversary, the most prominent opponent.

clue.text: Copy appeal held in India and China

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: the appeal word is held inside the other letters

parts.note: china is cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate)
it means sex appeal, as in 'she has it'

explanation.surface: Reproduce a petition lodged in two Asian nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: rhyming slang china plate = mate, i.e. friend. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone is to mimic or ape them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Other dodgy quote recalled is impractical

indicators.note: dodgy suggests something unsound, so the letters of the word are rearranged
recalled read as called back, so the word for quote runs backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: Another suspect quotation that was remembered can't be put into practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dodgy' rearranges OTHER into THEOR; 'recalled' turns CITE into ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something abstract and speculative rather than practical is a matter of theory alone.

clue.text: Old books kept by unknown round and rough type

indicators.note: the old books are kept inside the outer letters

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown
O is round in shape
B is book, so BB is books

explanation.surface: Antique volumes held by a stranger, complete with a rough ruffian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link word; YO is split around OBB.
explanation.definitionFit: A loutish, uncouth youth is British slang for a hooligan.

clue.text: Actor by the sound of it studied old director

indicators.note: this phrase says a spoken form is wanted, a past-tense verb as heard

parts.note: read, in the past tense, means studied (as in 'read law')
John Ford was a classic Hollywood film director

explanation.surface: A performer who apparently studied under a veteran film-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, star of Butch Cassidy and The Sting, is a famous Hollywood film star.

clue.text: Busy joint entertaining unworldly visitor taking in a lot of college

indicators.note: a host entertains guests within, so the joint holds the rest

parts.note: a dive is a seedy bar or club

indicators.note: the alien encloses the shortened college

parts.note: ET is the extraterrestrial of the film

indicators.note: most but not all of the word, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a tech is a technical college

explanation.surface: A crowded bar hosting an alien who's studied at a technical college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is British police slang for a plain-clothes officer, not 'occupied'. 'a lot of' cuts TECH to TEC.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a busy is a police investigator, a plain-clothes officer.

clue.text: Easterner having stored letter abroad?

parts.note: a native of a Himalayan land; a foreign alphabet's second letter is kept inside a metal container

explanation.surface: An Oriental man who has kept a letter while overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger reads BETA (a letter abroad, Greek) stored in TIN, but no clue word gives TIN, so the whole clue works as a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the high plateau north of the Himalayas lives in the East.

clue.text: Predatory type, Republican, inhibited by Obama largely — and group traditionally opposed to Republicans

indicators.note: the R is hemmed in by the shortened first name
most of the name, last letter dropped

parts.note: Barack is Obama's first name
the Ulster Defence Association, a loyalist paramilitary group opposed to Irish republicans

explanation.surface: A cut-throat Republican held back by the president and the party opposing him.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'Republicans' means Irish republicans, not the US party. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, sharp-toothed tropical fish that hunts its prey, a predator.

clue.text: One exhibited mobile with a paper? Not for all to see

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for mobile

indicators.note: not here means without, so that letter is removed

parts.note: tissue is thin paper
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: An exhibit features a hanging mobile and a newspaper that's not suitable for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word. A U film is universal, for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: The French painter's works hang in galleries, so he is an artist on show.

clue.text: Buggy in room ending in havoc? That's foolish

indicators.note: buggy suggests something faulty, full of errors, so the letters are jumbled
the final letter of the word havoc

explanation.surface: A pushchair inside a room ends up in chaos: that's silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buggy' rearranges IN ROOM into MORONI. 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid or idiotic behaviour is something only a dimwit would do.

clue.text: Key function in America for old currency

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

indicators.note: the function word goes inside the country abbreviation

parts.note: US is America
a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: An important function held in the States for an obsolete currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal's former money unit, replaced by the euro, is a currency of the past.

clue.text: Top Catholic about to meet Welsh group giving aid for flight

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
RC is Roman Catholic
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A senior Catholic meets a Welsh team to help the escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to meet' is a link. A1 (top-notch) is spelt AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The crew of an aircraft help the plane fly, assisting the flight.

clue.text: Arab and Irish politician accompanied by novelist in curvy style?

parts.note: Ar. is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic
a TD (Teachta Dala) is a member of the Irish parliament
Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: An Arab and an Irish MP, joined by an author, in a shapely fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'accompanied by' are links. The '?' marks the definition as loose: the style is better known for geometric lines.
explanation.definitionFit: An early-twentieth-century decorative design style, with stylised streamlined shapes.

clue.text: Royal's first person to get harsh vehicle for 13?

parts.note: the royal 'we' is the monarch's first-person pronoun
stern means severe or harsh

explanation.surface: The monarch's top man has a severe car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vehicle' means a film showcasing a star; 13 across is Redford, who starred in cowboy films.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy film was a showcase for Robert Redford, e.g. Butch Cassidy.

clue.text: Summary withdrawal of one first in field?

indicators.note: a withdrawal goes back, so the word runs in reverse

parts.note: a pacemaker in a race sets the pace at the front of the field

explanation.surface: A brief account of one leader pulling out of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief restatement of main points is a summing-up, a precis.

clue.text: Fish put in hamper chosen

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words hamper chosen

explanation.surface: A selected fish placed in a basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater fish with spiny fins, common in European rivers.

clue.text: Emotional release achieved by medieval Christian with female relative

parts.note: the Cathars were a medieval Christian sect in southern France
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A heretic and his sister find inner relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieved by' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Purging pent-up feeling, as in Greek tragedy, gives emotional relief.

clue.text: Mystic colleague from Bordeaux?

parts.note: the city lies in south-west France, abbreviated SW
ami is French for friend or companion

explanation.surface: A spiritual friend from south-west France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link: Bordeaux's position gives SW, and a French colleague is AMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hindu religious teacher or holy man is a spiritual guru.

clue.text: Strip of iron giving trouble on board deck with backing amateur removed

indicators.note: the trouble goes aboard, inside the other letters
backing means moving backwards, so the trimmed word runs in reverse
removed means the amateur's letter is taken away

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or decorate
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A metal bar causing problems on a ship's deck after the amateur is dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deck' looks like a ship's deck beside 'on board', but it is the verb meaning decorate. 'removed' leaves DORN and 'backing' turns it into NROD.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar of iron from which nails are cut is a metal rod used in smithing.

clue.text: Match delayed after one associated with Hull

indicators.note: the delay word comes after the bird

parts.note: Emu was the puppet of British entertainer Rod Hull
late means delayed

explanation.surface: A game postponed after a Hull City player.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is not the city but Rod Hull, the British TV entertainer famous for his aggressive puppet Emu.
explanation.definitionFit: To equal or rival someone is to try to match their achievement.

clue.text: Old European zoo can veil shack that's rickety

indicators.note: rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A zoo can conceal a dilapidated shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the former central European state that split in 1993 belonged to an old nation.
